description:
FILED s473u (2026-09-08, Opus) â the next lever the gate profile names, measured
but NOT built.  Sizing below; nothing here is a bug.

After #1544 (the 25 files that recompiled the runtime on every row) and #1545
(the transpile server), one full gate on the s473u tree is **86.1 s wall /
394.7 CPU-s**, from 463 s / 2933 CPU-s.  What is LEFT, from the `--timer` log of
that run (`tools/gate-profile.pl`), is 226 timed files summing to 655.6 s of
per-file wall, with a long flat tail and this head:

    cache-surface-01.t        41.2 s   <- the gate's WALL FLOOR at -j8
    moo-01.t                  28.9
    module-fasl-cache-01.t    26.3
    socket-01.t               23.1
    use-require-01.t          11.9
    tap-assert-01.t           11.8
    eval-cache-01.t           11.6
    local-paren-begin-do-01.t 11.2
    transpile-test-04.t       11.1
    misc-fixes-01.t           10.8

TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS, and they want different answers:

(a) THE WALL FLOOR.  `prove -j8` parallelises across FILES, so the gate's wall
can never go below its slowest single file â 41.2 s today, against 86.1 s
measured, so there is roughly a factor of two of scheduling headroom and then a
hard stop.  The four heads (cache-surface, moo, module-fasl-cache, socket) are
all files whose rows deliberately exercise the MODULE CACHE or a subprocess
protocol, i.e. their cost is the thing they test.  The cheap move is not to make
them faster but to let prove start them FIRST (`prove --rules` / a slowest-first
ordering from the profile the instrument already prints); the expensive move is
splitting them, which changes what a file asserts and is not obviously worth it.

(b) THE CPU.  394.7 CPU-s over ~7780 rows is ~50 ms a row, and the fixed
transpile cost is now ~0 (the server) and SBCL start ~7 ms (the saved core).
What remains per row is the compile-load of the emitted CL inside sbcl, which is
real work, plus the module-cache reads.  Measuring THAT split (compile-load vs
cache I/O vs the program's own run) is the next profile, and it needs a
different instrument from `tools/gate-profile.pl`: per-row timing from inside
the sbcl process, not per-file wall from prove.

NOT DONE BECAUSE: the s473u brief licensed only the levers its own table named,
and this one needs a measurement the table does not contain.  Do (b)'s
measurement before building anything â the s473u finding was that the lever
everyone assumed (SBCL start) was worth 22 CPU-s of 2933, while the one nobody
had looked at was worth 1527.
subject: The gate after s473u: 86 s wall / 395 CPU-s, floored by cache-surface-01.t at 41 s â the next lever is (a) slowest-first file ordering and (b) a per-ROW profile from inside sbcl, measured before anything is built
